salient_findings: Pulsatile mass in the epigastric region
key_facts: 84-year-old man with medical history of hyperlipidemia, hypertension, hypothyroidism, and tobacco use
20-pack-year smoking history
Smoking pipe tobacco for the past 10 years
Asymptomatic abdominal mass with pulsations
Vital signs: Temperature - afebrile, Blood pressure - 120/76 mm Hg, Pulse rate - 73 beats/min, Respiratory rate - 16/minute
Pulses were palpable in the lower extremities bilaterally
Complete blood count and electrolyte levels were within normal limits
Computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm
Aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees with neck tortuosity noted
Dense calcifications of iliac vessels present without narrowing
No signs of impending rupture

shortlist.label: Abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Large pulsatile mass in epigastric region with soft bruit and imaging showing saccular aneurysm

shortlist.label: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of dense calcifications and aneurysmal neck angulation greater than 60 degrees

shortlist.label: Common iliac artery aneurysm
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging showing aneurysm in abdominal region and patient's smoking history

shortlist.label: Aortoiliac occlusive disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's smoking history and presence of dense calcifications in iliac vessels

raw.rationale: The patient's computed tomographic angiogram (CTA) of abdomen and pelvis showed a saccular aneurysm measuring 14.6 cm × 12.6 cm, which is consistent with an abdominal aortic aneurysm. The patient's long history of smoking and hypertension also increases the risk of developing an abdominal aortic aneurysm.

rejected.label: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm
rejected.why: There is no mention of inflammatory symptoms or signs, such as fever, elevated white blood cell count, or periaortic fibrosis, which are characteristic of inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm.

rejected.label: Common iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: The CTA showed a saccular aneurysm in the abdominal aorta, not in the common iliac artery.

rejected.label: Internal iliac artery aneurysm
rejected.why: The CTA showed a saccular aneurysm in the abdominal aorta, not in the internal iliac artery.

rejected.label: Aortoiliac occlusive disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with an aneurysm rather than occlusive disease, and there is no mention of significant stenosis or occlusion of the aortoiliac vessels.
